points.title: 童年与家庭
points.description: 1821年4月9日，夏尔·波德莱尔出生于巴黎。他的父亲是老约瑟夫-弗朗索瓦·波德莱尔，一位退休外交官和艺术家；母亲是卡罗琳·杜菲诺，出身于普通家庭。波德莱尔7岁时父亲去世，母亲随后改嫁雅克·奥比克上校。这段经历使波德莱尔对家庭关系产生了复杂情感，也影响了他后来的创作主题。童年时期，波德莱尔展现出对艺术的敏感和天赋，尤其喜爱绘画和诗歌。
points.descriptionEn: Charles Baudelaire was born in Paris on April 9, 1821. His father, Joseph-François Baudelaire, was a retired diplomat and artist; his mother, Caroline Dufaÿ, came from a modest family. When Baudelaire was seven, his father died, and his mother later remarried Jacques Aupick, an army officer. This experience created complex feelings about family relationships that influenced his later themes. During his childhood, Baudelaire showed sensitivity and talent for the arts, particularly painting and poetry.

points.title: 青年叛逆期
points.description: 1839年，波德莱尔进入路易大帝中学学习，但表现出强烈的叛逆倾向。他拒绝服从继父的权威，生活放荡不羁，沉迷于酒精和享乐主义。1841年，在继父的安排下，波德莱尔被送往印度航行，希望这次旅行能改变他的生活方式。然而，他在毛里求斯岛中途下船，提前返回巴黎。这段经历虽然短暂，但为他后来的创作提供了异域色彩的素材，也加深了他对自由的渴望和对束缚的反抗。
points.descriptionEn: In 1839, Baudelaire entered the Lycée Louis-le-Grand, but showed strong rebellious tendencies. He refused to submit to his stepfather's authority and lived a dissolute life, indulging in alcohol and hedonism. In 1841, arranged by his stepfather, Baudelaire was sent on a voyage to India, hoping this journey would change his lifestyle. However, he disembarked at Mauritius and returned to Paris prematurely. Although brief, this experience provided exotic material for his later works and deepened his longing for freedom and rebellion against constraints.

points.title: 文学创作高峰
points.description: 1845年后，波德莱尔开始专注于文学创作，成为巴黎文学圈的重要人物。他翻译了美国作家爱伦·坡的作品，深受其影响。1848年，他参与革命活动，创办了《公共安全》杂志。1857年，他发表了代表作《恶之花》，这部诗集因其大胆的主题和创新的风格引起巨大争议，甚至被法院判为有伤风化。这一时期，波德莱尔还撰写了大量艺术评论，推崇德拉克洛瓦等浪漫主义画家，对现代艺术批评的发展做出了重要贡献。
points.descriptionEn: After 1845, Baudelaire focused on literary creation and became an important figure in Parisian literary circles. He translated works by American writer Edgar Allan Poe, who deeply influenced him. In 1848, he participated in revolutionary activities and founded the magazine 'La Tribune publique.' In 1857, he published his masterpiece 'Les Fleurs du Mal' (The Flowers of Evil), which caused huge controversy for its bold themes and innovative style, even leading to a court ruling for indecency. During this period, Baudelaire also wrote numerous art critiques, promoting Romantic painters like Delacroix, making significant contributions to the development of modern art criticism.

points.title: 流亡与创作转型
points.description: 1857年，《恶之花》出版后引发争议，波德莱尔开始考虑离开巴黎。1861年，他移居布鲁塞尔，试图寻找新的创作环境。在布鲁塞尔期间，他继续写作，但生活日益贫困，健康状况恶化。他开始创作散文诗集《巴黎的忧郁》，并计划新的诗歌集。这一时期，波德莱尔对艺术的思考更加深入，开始探索现代城市生活的复杂性，以及艺术与社会的关系。他的创作风格也变得更加内省和哲学化。
points.descriptionEn: After the publication of 'Les Fleurs du Mal' in 1857 sparked controversy, Baudelaire began considering leaving Paris. In 1861, he moved to Brussels, seeking a new creative environment. During his time in Brussels, he continued writing but his life became increasingly impoverished and his health deteriorated. He began writing 'Le Spleen de Paris' (The Parisian Pity) and planned a new poetry collection. During this period, Baudelaire's reflections on art deepened, exploring the complexity of modern urban life and the relationship between art and society. His writing style became more introspective and philosophical.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 1864年，波德莱尔返回巴黎，但健康状况已严重恶化，生活贫困潦倒。1866年，他因中风导致半身不遂，1867年8月31日在巴黎逝世，年仅46岁。波德莱尔生前并未获得广泛认可，但去世后，他的作品逐渐被重新评价，对现代主义文学产生了深远影响。他的《恶之花》被视为现代诗歌的里程碑，影响了后来的象征主义、超现实主义等文学流派。波德莱尔对现代城市生活的描绘、对邪恶与美的探索，以及对艺术独立性的坚持，使他成为现代文学和艺术批评的重要先驱。
points.descriptionEn: In 1864, Baudelaire returned to Paris, but his health had severely deteriorated and he lived in poverty. In 1866, he suffered a stroke that left him partially paralyzed, and on August 31, 1867, he died in Paris at the age of 46. Baudelaire did not gain wide recognition during his lifetime, but after his death, his works were re-evaluated and had a profound influence on modernist literature. 'Les Fleurs du Mal' is considered a milestone of modern poetry, influencing later literary movements such as Symbolism and Surrealism. Baudelaire's depictions of modern urban life, exploration of evil and beauty, and insistence on artistic independence made him an important pioneer of modern literature and art criticism.

appraisal.zh: 波德莱尔通常被视为现代主义文学的先驱和象征主义诗歌的奠基人，《恶之花》把现代都市生活的复杂与矛盾引入诗歌，对恶与美的辩证探索及对艺术独立性的坚持为后世开辟道路，其影响更延伸至视觉艺术、音乐与哲学。不过也有研究者指出其创作过于颓废病态、风格晦涩难懂，对爱伦·坡的模仿明显而缺乏原创，生活方式亦被视为道德堕落。总体而言，他仍被公认为现代性的重要诠释者。
appraisal.en: Baudelaire is generally seen as a pioneer of modernist literature and a founder of Symbolist poetry: 'Les Fleurs du Mal' brought the complexity and contradictions of modern urban life into verse, and his dialectical exploration of evil and beauty and his insistence on artistic independence opened the way for later modernism, with influence extending into visual art, music and philosophy. Yet some researchers point to a morbid, decadent sensibility, an obscure style inaccessible to ordinary readers, an imitation of Poe that lacks originality, and a lifestyle condemned as morally corrupt. On balance he is still recognized as a key interpreter of modernity.

supporter.zh: 波德莱尔被视为现代主义文学的先驱和象征主义诗歌的奠基人。他的《恶之花》打破了传统诗歌的界限，将现代城市生活的复杂性和矛盾性引入诗歌创作。波德莱尔对邪恶与美的辩证探索，以及对艺术独立性的坚持，为后来的现代主义文学开辟了道路。他敏锐地捕捉了现代性体验，将巴黎的城市景观转化为艺术意象，影响了无数后来的作家和艺术家。波德莱尔的作品体现了艺术家的社会责任感和对真理的不懈追求，成为现代文学不可或缺的经典。
supporter.en: Baudelaire is regarded as a pioneer of modernist literature and a founder of Symbolist poetry. His 'Les Fleurs du Mal' broke the boundaries of traditional poetry, introducing the complexity and contradictions of modern urban life into poetic creation. Baudelaire's dialectical exploration of evil and beauty, and his insistence on artistic independence, paved the way for later modernist literature. He keenly captured modern experiences, transforming Parisian urban landscapes into artistic imagery, influencing countless subsequent writers and artists. His works embody the artist's social responsibility and relentless pursuit of truth, becoming indispensable classics of modern literature.

critic.zh: 批评者认为波德莱尔的创作过于颓废和病态，过分关注阴暗面而缺乏积极意义。他的生活方式被指责为道德堕落，对酒精和毒品的依赖影响了他的创作质量。一些评论家认为波德莱尔对爱伦·坡的模仿过于明显，缺乏原创性。此外，他对现代性的悲观态度和对传统价值的拒绝，也被视为对社会的消极影响。波德莱尔的晦涩风格和复杂意象也被批评为脱离大众，使他的作品难以被普通读者理解和接受。
critic.en: Critics argue that Baudelaire's work is excessively decadent and morbid, focusing too much on the dark side without positive meaning. His lifestyle was condemned as morally corrupt, and his dependence on alcohol and drugs affected the quality of his work. Some critics believe his imitation of Edgar Allan Poe was too obvious and lacked originality. Additionally, his pessimistic attitude toward modernity and rejection of traditional values were seen as having a negative impact on society. Baudelaire's obscure style and complex imagery were also criticized as being inaccessible to ordinary readers, making his works difficult to understand and accept.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，波德莱尔被定义为现代性的重要诠释者和象征主义文学的代表人物。他的作品反映了19世纪巴黎的社会变革和文化转型，捕捉了现代都市生活的疏离感和矛盾性。波德莱尔对艺术与社会关系的思考，以及对艺术家角色的重新定义，使他成为现代艺术批评的重要先驱。在流行文化中，波德莱尔的形象常与颓废、唯美和波西米亚生活方式联系在一起，成为反叛精神和艺术自由的象征。他的影响超越了文学领域，延伸到视觉艺术、音乐和哲学等多个领域，塑造了现代艺术的基本特征。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Baudelaire is defined as an important interpreter of modernity and a representative figure of Symbolist literature. His work reflects the social changes and cultural transformation of 19th-century Paris, capturing the sense of alienation and contradiction in modern urban life. Baudelaire's reflections on the relationship between art and society, and his redefinition of the artist's role, make him an important precursor of modern art criticism. In popular culture, Baudelaire's image is often associated with decadence, aestheticism, and bohemian lifestyles, becoming a symbol of rebellious spirit and artistic freedom. His influence extends beyond literature into visual arts, music, and philosophy, shaping the fundamental characteristics of modern art.

self.zh: 现代性就是短暂的、易逝的、偶然的，是艺术的一半，另一半是永恒和不变。
self.en: Modernity is the transient, the fleeting, the contingent; it is one half of art, the other half being the eternal and immutable.
